nfce018c0cf7.s: The third (local) tier of government was added to India's original dual polity by the:
nfce018c0cf7.x: The 73rd (Panchayats) and 74th (Municipalities) Amendments of 1992 created the third tier; the 97th Amendment (2011) added Part IXB on Co-operative Societies.

n806d44b5cb8.s: The critics' description of the Indian Constitution as 'elephantine' refers to its:
n806d44b5cb8.x: 'Elephantine' criticises the great length and bulk of the Constitution; 'lawyers' paradise', 'borrowed constitution' and 'carbon copy of the 1935 Act' are the other criticisms.

n6974eb8880f.s: Unlike the British Parliament, the Indian Parliament is:
o: Bound by a written Constitution and judicial review
Free from the limits of Fundamental Rights
n6974eb8880f.x: The Indian Parliament is not sovereign in the British sense: it is bound by a written Constitution, Fundamental Rights and judicial review.

n4efbe1ada9f.s: With respect to religion, the Indian Constitution establishes India as a:
o: Secular state with no state religion
n4efbe1ada9f.x: India is a secular state and has no state religion; a religious or theocratic state is not a feature of the Constitution.

nfccdb21f4ef.s: How many Schedules did the original Constitution of India contain?
nfccdb21f4ef.x: The original Constitution had 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules; there are 12 Schedules now.

n4bd5a3d9e25.s: The idea of having a Preamble in the Indian Constitution was taken from the Constitution of:
n4bd5a3d9e25.x: The idea of a Preamble and 'We, the people' come from the US Constitution; its language is credited to Australia.

n191f2bac169.s: The term 'Democratic' in the Preamble covers:
n191f2bac169.x: 'Democratic' in the Preamble is not limited to political democracy; it covers social and economic democracy as well.

n3a302a8dd46.s: Secularism became a part of the basic structure of the Constitution:
o: Even before the word 'Secular' was inserted in 1976
Only when the 42nd Amendment inserted 'Secular' in 1976
Only after the Balram Singh judgment, 2024
n3a302a8dd46.x: Secularism was part of the basic structure even before the word 'Secular' was inserted by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.

nindian-polity-24-7.s: Minerva Mills (1980) struck down 42nd Amendment clauses that gave absolute precedence over Fundamental Rights to the:
nindian-polity-24-7.x: Minerva Mills struck down the clauses giving DPSPs absolute priority over Fundamental Rights, restoring the balance of Parts III and IV and reinforcing the basic structure.

nindian-polity-6-6.s: How many Parts does the Constitution of India have at present?
nindian-polity-6-6.x: The Constitution originally had 22 Parts and has 25 now: Parts IVA, IXA, IXB and XIVA were added later and Part VII was repealed.

nindian-polity-6-11.s: Part IX-A of the Constitution, dealing with the Municipalities, covers Articles:
nindian-polity-6-11.x: Part IXA (Municipalities) covers Articles 243P-243ZG; Part IX covers 243-243O and Part IXB (Co-operative Societies, 97th Amendment, 2011) covers 243ZH-243ZT. No dated order can be built, so a one-liner is used.

nindian-polity-6-12.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Parts X and XI of the Constitution?
o: Part X deals with Scheduled and Tribal Areas
Part X was in the original Constitution
Part XI was added later by an amendment
nindian-polity-6-12.x: Both Part X (Articles 244-244A) and Part XI (Relations between the Union and the States, Articles 245-263) were in the original Constitution, so Part XI was not added later.

nindian-polity-6-17.s: Part XVII (Articles 343-351) of the Constitution deals with:
o: Special provisions relating to certain classes
nindian-polity-6-17.x: Part XVII (Articles 343-351) deals with the Official Language; Emergency provisions are in Part XVIII.

nindian-polity-2-56.s: Articles 330-334 of the Constitution deal with:
o: Reservation of seats for SCs, STs and Anglo-Indians
nindian-polity-2-56.x: Articles 330-334 deal with reservation of seats for SCs, STs and Anglo-Indians; Official Language is in Articles 343-351.

nindian-polity-5-2-4.s: The Fourth Schedule of the Constitution deals with:
o: Names and territories of States and UTs
nindian-polity-5-2-4.x: The Fourth Schedule allocates Rajya Sabha seats; the anti-defection law is in the Tenth Schedule.

nindian-polity-5-2-6.s: The tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram are dealt with in the:
nindian-polity-5-2-6.x: The Sixth Schedule covers the tribal areas of these four north-eastern States; the Fifth deals with Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.

nindian-polity-5-2-11.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Lists in the Seventh Schedule?
o: The Union List originally had 97 subjects
The State List now has 61 subjects
The State List originally had 47 subjects
The Concurrent List now has 52 subjects
nindian-polity-5-2-11.x: The State List originally had 66 subjects (now 61); 47 was the original count of the Concurrent List (now 52).

nindian-polity-48-4.s: Under Article 371-A, Parliament's laws on Naga customary law and land ownership apply to Nagaland only if:
nindian-polity-48-4.x: Article 371-A shields Naga customs, customary justice and land ownership from Parliament's laws unless the Nagaland Assembly agrees.

new.s: Who described the Indian Constitution as 'quasi-federal'?
new.x: K.C. Wheare called it quasi-federal, a unitary state with federal features; 'elephantine' was H.V. Kamath's description.

new.s: Who said the Indian Constitution can be unitary or federal as time and circumstances require?
new.x: B.R. Ambedkar said the Constitution can be unitary or federal according to time and circumstances.

new.s: The term 'cooperative federalism' for the Indian Constitution is associated with:
new.x: Granville Austin called it cooperative federalism; Jennings saw a strong centralising tendency and Morris-Jones bargaining federalism.

new.s: Which pair of Indian constitutional feature and the country it was borrowed from is correctly matched?
new.x: The amendment procedure came from South Africa; the Concurrent List is from Australia, a strong Centre from Canada and the parliamentary system from Britain.

new.s: New Articles added to the Constitution, such as 21A and 51A, show that the numbering still ends at Article:
new.x: New provisions are added as lettered Articles, so the numbering still ends at Article 395.

new.s: Which Act heavily influenced the Indian Constitution and added to its length?
new.x: The heavy influence of the Government of India Act, 1935 is one reason for the Constitution's length.

new.s: Which is the only Part of the Constitution to have been repealed?
new.x: Part VII was repealed by the 7th Amendment, 1956; IVA and XIVA were added by the 42nd Amendment.

new.s: Part VIII of the Constitution deals with:
new.x: Part VIII deals with Union Territories; Part II is Citizenship, Part V the Union and Part XVIII Emergency Provisions.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Parts added to the Constitution:
1. Part IVA (Fundamental Duties) was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
2. Part XIVA (Tribunals) was added by the 74th Amendment, 1992.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Part IVA came by the 42nd Amendment (1976); Part XIVA (Tribunals) was also added by the 42nd, while the 74th added Part IXA (Municipalities).

new.s: The Council of Ministers in India is collectively responsible to the:
new.x: Under Articles 74(1) and 75 the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's parliamentary system?
o: Ministers are members of the legislature
Britain's head of State is elected
India's head of State is elected indirectly
new.x: Britain's head of State is hereditary; it is India's head of State who is elected indirectly.

new.s: India's representative democracy at the national level does NOT have:
new.x: India is a representative (indirect) democracy with no referendum, initiative or recall at the national level.

new.s: Limits on government power in India include Article 13, under which:
o: Laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void
Parliament may amend any part freely
new.x: Article 13 makes laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights void, a key limit of constitutionalism in India.

new.s: The basic structure doctrine limiting Parliament's amending power came from which case?
new.x: The basic structure limit on Parliament's amending power comes from Kesavananda Bharati (1973).

new.s: The Union and the State governments in India derive their powers from the:
new.x: The Constitution is the supreme law, and both the Union and the States derive their powers from it.

new.s: The supreme authority in the Indian political system is the:
new.x: The Constitution, not Parliament, is the supreme authority; the ultimate source of authority is 'We, the People of India'.

new.s: Which of the following is a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution?
new.x: Single citizenship is a unitary feature; division of powers, bicameralism and a written Constitution are federal features.

new.s: In an emergency, the federal structure of India becomes unitary:
o: Only with ratification by half the States
Only by a Supreme Court order
new.x: In an emergency the federal structure turns unitary without any formal amendment.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Indian federalism:
1. Indian States have no separate constitutions.
2. India has dual citizenship like the USA.
3. The strong Centre is modelled on Canada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: States have no separate constitutions and the strong Centre follows Canada; India has single citizenship, not the dual citizenship of the USA.

new.s: Admission of new States into the Union requires an amendment by:
o: Special majority and ratification by half the States
new.x: Admission of new States and changes of State boundaries need only a simple majority of Parliament, outside Article 368.

new.s: Federal provisions of the Constitution are amended by a special majority of Parliament plus ratification by:
new.x: Federal provisions need a special majority of Parliament and ratification by half the State legislatures.

new.s: Most provisions of the Constitution, such as Fundamental Rights, are amended under Article 368 by:
new.x: Most provisions, including Fundamental Rights, are amended by a special majority of Parliament under Article 368.

new.s: The Indian model of secularism is described as:
o: Strict separation of State and religion
Positive, with equal respect for all religions
new.x: The Indian (positive) model gives equal respect to all religions; strict separation is the Western (negative) model.

new.s: Freedom of religion is guaranteed under Articles:
new.x: Freedom of religion is in Articles 25-28.

new.s: The Indian judiciary is a synthesis of parliamentary sovereignty of Britain and:
new.x: India combines British parliamentary sovereignty with American judicial supremacy: courts can strike down laws.

new.s: During a National Emergency, which Fundamental Rights cannot be suspended?
new.x: All Fundamental Rights can be suspended in a National Emergency except Articles 20 and 21.

new.s: How many Fundamental Duties are there in the Constitution at present?
new.x: There are 11 Fundamental Duties: ten by the 42nd Amendment and one added by the 86th.

new.s: Which of the following is an independent constitutional body?
new.x: Independent bodies include the ECI, CAG, UPSC and SPSCs.

new.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Indian Constitution?
new.x: Dual citizenship is the odd one out (APPSC GS 2025); India has single citizenship.

new.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Indian Constitution?
new.x: Presidential government is not a feature; India has a parliamentary form.

new.s: Which one of the following is a feature of the Indian Constitution?
new.x: Division of powers is a feature; a hereditary head, an unwritten constitution and property-based franchise are non-features.

new.s: The Objectives Resolution, the basis of the Preamble, was moved by:
new.x: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946; its modified version became the Preamble.

new.s: The Objectives Resolution was moved in the Constituent Assembly on:
new.x: It was moved on 13 December 1946 and adopted unanimously on 22 January 1947.

new.s: The ideal of Justice – social, economic and political – in the Preamble is drawn from the:
new.x: Justice (social, economic, political) comes from the Russian Revolution (1917); Liberty, Equality, Fraternity from the French Revolution (1789).

new.s: The language of the Preamble is credited to the Constitution of:
new.x: The language of the Preamble is credited to Australia; the idea of a Preamble comes from the USA.

new.s: Which of the following words is NOT found in the Preamble?
new.x: The Preamble uses Liberty, Equality, Justice and Fraternity; the word 'Freedom' is not used.

new.s: In the original 1949 Preamble, the fraternity clause spoke of assuring the:
o: Unity and integrity of the Nation
new.x: The original said 'unity of the Nation'; 'integrity' was added in 1976.

new.s: According to its meaning in the Preamble, 'Sovereign' means India is:
new.x: Sovereign means supreme authority, internally and externally free; the others describe Republic, Secular and Socialist.

new.s: The 'Socialist' character of the Indian State leans towards:
new.x: Indian socialism is democratic socialism, a blend of Marxism and Gandhism leaning towards Gandhian socialism.

new.s: How many kinds of liberty does the Preamble name?
new.x: Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship – five kinds.

new.s: Liberty, as meant in the Preamble, is:
o: Absence of restraints plus opportunities to develop personality
new.x: Liberty means absence of restraints on individual activity plus opportunities to develop personality, not freedom from every restraint.

new.s: Fraternity in the Indian context is promoted by:
new.x: Fraternity, a sense of brotherhood, is promoted by single citizenship.

new.s: The Kesavananda Bharati case was decided by a bench of how many judges?
new.x: A 13-judge bench gave the Basic Structure doctrine in 1973 and held the Preamble a part of the Constitution.

new.s: Which case of 1995 reaffirmed that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution?
new.x: LIC of India (1995) reaffirmed the Preamble as an integral part of the Constitution.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Preamble?
o: It is an aid to interpreting ambiguous provisions
It is a source of power to the legislature
new.x: The Preamble is neither a source of power nor a limit on express powers.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Preamble:
1. It can be enforced in a court of law.
2. It is used as an aid to interpretation where a provision is ambiguous.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Preamble is non-justiciable but serves as an aid to interpretation of ambiguous provisions.

new.s: According to Kesavananda Bharati, the Preamble is amendable under Article 368, but:
o: Its basic features cannot be destroyed
Only with ratification by all States
new.x: Kesavananda Bharati held the Preamble amendable under Article 368, but its basic features cannot be destroyed.

new.s: Waman Rao (1981) held that basic-structure review applies to amendments made after:
new.x: Waman Rao applied basic-structure review to amendments made after 24 April 1973.

new.s: Which case held that a State government acting against secularism could be dismissed?
new.x: S.R. Bommai (1994) held secularism a basic feature, so a State government acting against it could be dismissed.

new.s: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 was based on the recommendations of the:
new.x: The 42nd Amendment was based on the Swaran Singh Committee and is called the Mini Constitution.

new.s: Which word in the Preamble was added by the 42nd Amendment?
new.x: Integrity was added in 1976; Fraternity, Sovereign and Republic were in the original text.

new.s: Who called the Preamble the 'identity card' of the Constitution?
new.x: N.A. Palkhivala called it the identity card; K.M. Munshi called it the political horoscope.

new.s: Ambedkar's phrase 'heart and soul' of the Constitution refers to:
new.x: Ambedkar called Article 32 the heart and soul, not the Preamble.

new.s: Who described the Preamble as the 'key-note' to the Constitution?
new.x: Ernest Barker called the Preamble the key-note to the Constitution.

new.s: How many Schedules does the Constitution have at present?
new.x: 8 original Schedules plus 4 added (Ninth to Twelfth) make 12.

new.s: Part XII of the Constitution deals with:
o: Services under the Union and States
new.x: Part XII (Articles 264-300A) covers Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits.

new.s: Which Part of the Constitution deals with Elections?
new.x: Part XV (Articles 324-329A) deals with Elections.

new.s: Article 2A relating to Sikkim was inserted by the 35th Amendment and omitted by the:
new.x: Article 2A was inserted by the 35th and omitted by the 36th Amendment.

new.s: Article 329A was omitted by the:
new.x: Article 329A was omitted by the 44th Amendment.

new.s: Part VII of the Constitution was repealed by the:
new.x: Part VII (Part B States) was repealed by the 7th Amendment (1956), not the 44th.

new.s: The Eleventh Schedule contains how many matters for Panchayats?
new.x: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 matters for Panchayats; the Twelfth lists 18 for Municipalities.

new.s: The Twelfth Schedule, listing 18 matters of Municipalities, was added by the:
new.x: The 74th Amendment (1992) added the Twelfth Schedule; the 73rd added the Eleventh.

new.s: The Tenth Schedule (anti-defection) was added by the:
new.x: The Tenth Schedule came with the 52nd Amendment, 1985.

new.s: The Tenth Schedule was changed by the 91st Amendment (2003), which removed the:
new.x: The 91st Amendment removed the 'split' exception from the anti-defection law.

new.s: Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after which date are open to judicial review?
new.x: The Supreme Court (2007) held laws added after 24 April 1973 open to judicial review.

new.s: The 71st Amendment (1992) added which languages to the Eighth Schedule?
new.x: The 71st added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; Maithili came with the 92nd.

new.s: Maithili was added to the Eighth Schedule by the:
new.x: The 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali.

new.s: The oath of office of a Governor is prescribed by:
new.x: The Governor's oath is under Article 159, outside the Third Schedule.

new.s: Which of the following oaths is NOT in the Third Schedule?
new.x: The President's oath is in Article 60, not the Third Schedule.

new.s: A Money Bill is defined in Article:
new.x: Article 110 defines a Money Bill; Article 123 is the President's ordinance power.

new.s: The ordinance-making power of the President is in Article:
new.x: Article 123 gives the President ordinance power.

new.s: The advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is under Article:
new.x: Article 143 gives the Supreme Court advisory jurisdiction (borrowed from Canada).

new.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
new.x: Article 356 is President's Rule; 368 is amendment, 324 the Election Commission and 280 the Finance Commission.

new.s: Article 371H gives the Governor special responsibility for law and order in:
new.x: Article 371H concerns Arunachal Pradesh and the Governor's responsibility for law and order.

new.s: Article 371E of the Constitution provides for:
o: Equitable opportunities in public employment in AP
A Central University in Andhra Pradesh
new.x: Article 371E provides for a Central University in Andhra Pradesh by law of Parliament; 371D deals with equitable opportunities.

new.s: Article 371C provides for an Assembly committee of members from the Hill areas of:
new.x: Article 371C concerns Manipur's Hill areas; 371B is the tribal-areas committee of Assam.
